scope: Read-only local isolated recovery preparation; no retained overwrite, actual restore, key read, cleanup or application reopen.

helper.entrypoint: prepare(manifest, archive=path, storage_snapshot=path, key_inventory=id_to_path, target_id=token, port=port, expected=ExpectedBackup)

trusted_expected_inventory.postgres_major: Strict integer >=16; exact manifest equality required. This is metadata compatibility, not installed-tool/runtime verification.
trusted_expected_inventory.key_ids: Nonempty frozenset of opaque IDs matching ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,80}$; no key bytes.
trusted_expected_inventory.trust: Must come from independently trusted inventory, not the backup manifest itself. No signatures/authenticity or actual decryption are established by equality checks alone.

manifest.hashes_and_version: Exact type/value agreement with trusted expected inventory.
manifest.key_ids: Unique list with exact trusted expected key-ID membership. Key inventory may contain additional files, but every required ID must resolve to an existing private file.

helper.inputs: Existing absolute canonical files under workspace .cache; no traversal, symlink/junction redirects or archive/storage/key file identity aliases including hardlinks. Stream-hash archive/storage in 1MiB chunks; never read key files.

target.existing_target: Refuse any existing directory/file/link even if a prior marker matches; never adopt or overwrite.
target.listener_check: Brief exclusive loopback bind where supported; occupied/unavailable resource fails. This is neither process adoption nor a reservation.

runtime_requirements: A separately scoped executor must atomically reserve a new uniquely owned workspace target/cluster/port/runtime context and reverify ownership, input digests and compatibility immediately before restore. Read-only preparation has a time-of-check/time-of-use gap.
Never touch existing unrelated PostgreSQL services or retained kapit_m1 data; existing targets and unknown processes/resources remain refused.

Backup may resurrect withdrawn outputs, revoked grants, sessions or keys. Without authoritative current revocation/policy/withdrawal evidence, remain CLOSED; backup alone cannot establish current authorization.
Rehearse actual restore and correct/missing/wrong-key decryption, relational guards, worker lease recovery, receipts/dedup and current scope denial; unit mocks prove guards only.
Keep failed isolated sandbox evidence. Any later cleanup requires a separate explicit ownership-verified procedure; never perform broad recursive cleanup.
Record actual backup age, restore/reconciliation elapsed duration and known data-loss window. RPO 24h/RTO 4h are proposed targets, not achieved results.
